source_text: Certe nulla hic de studiis adultorum hominum quaestio, sed de sola nascentium qualitate versatur, in quibus naturae examinatur status. Hanc tu itaque naturam sine aliquo propriae voluntatis admixtu ream, damnatam, malis id est criminibus plenam cum Manichaeo tamen asseris, quam nos sine scelere, sine peccati malo innoxiam et capacem virtutis tuemur.
pass_a_gloss: Certainly here there is no question of the studies of adult humans, but it is turned concerning the quality of those being born alone, in whom the status of nature is examined. This nature therefore you, without any mixture of its own will, defendant, condemned, full of evils that is of crimes, with the Manichaean nevertheless assert, which we without crime, without the evil of sin, guard harmless and capable of virtue.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Certainly the question here does not concern adults’ pursuits, but only the condition of newborns, in whom nature’s state is examined. Alongside Mani, you maintain that this nature, without any contribution from its own will, is guilty, condemned, and full of evils—that is, crimes. We defend it as guiltless, free from wickedness and the evil of sin, and capable of virtue.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
